beginner.headline: Today (Sun Oct 18): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–10:00 AM: light wind at Honolulu at 6 AM (E about 6 mph) and a rising tide toward the 10:31 AM high (1.8 ft). Trades are forecast to fill in to around 20 mph with gusty leeward downslope winds this afternoon. 10:00 AM–12:00 PM conditional; from noon not recommended.
beginner.recommendation: Go early and keep it flexible. Wind at 6 AM was much lighter in Honolulu (E 5 kt, about 6 mph) than at Kāneʻohe (E 15 gusting 28 kt), so the leeward side is sheltered for now, but NWS expects trades to strengthen today with gusty downslope winds on leeward sides this afternoon (surf zone forecast: E around 20 mph). The south-southwest swell is declining (NWS); the surf-forecast.com Waikīkī model has about 1.6 ft at 13 s this morning and a small 17 s SW component this afternoon. Small at Canoes, but long-period, so watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before committing. Overnight showers spilled over to leeward areas (NWS: 0.10–0.75 in on some leeward spots), so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side before going in. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only while drift stays low. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.statement: Part of the DOH Clean Water Branch brown-water list loaded (entries A–H alphabetically). In that part, the only open advisory is Anini Beach, Kauaʻi (Oct 13); Bellows to Sherwood (Oʻahu, Oct 9) and Ala Wai Boat Harbor (Aug 26) are closed. The rest of the brown-water list and the bacteria and sewage lists were not read, so Waikīkī and the North Shore advisories reported Oct 16 are not verified. Not finding an advisory does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: The DOH list loads only partly through the fetch tool and filtered queries are blocked. NWS reports overnight showers spilled to leeward areas (about 0.10–0.75 in on some leeward spots), which raises runoff risk at Waikīkī.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
